intro.cn: captive 直接来自拉丁语 captivus（俘虏），词根 capere 意为抓取。

items.en: Capere means to seize.
items.cn: capere 意为抓取。

items.en: Captivus means a prisoner.
items.cn: captivus 意为俘虏。

items.en: English captive names a prisoner of war.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语指战俘。

items.en: Captive is used before a noun, as captive bird.
items.cn: 十七世纪起作定语，如笼中鸟。

items.en: A captive market is one with no choice.
items.cn: 二十世纪出现「受制市场」之说。

items.en: Captive covers people, animals and audiences.
items.cn: 现代涵盖人、动物与听众。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the capt- root; the near-meaning group ranks people kept against their will from prisoner to detainee.
note.cn: 形近组共享 capt- 词根；近义组把被违背意愿扣留的人从囚犯排到被拘留者。

entries.definition: To catch and hold.
To hold attention completely.
Quick to find small faults.
Someone kept in prison or by captors.
Someone held to force another to act.
A person kept in a prison or hospital.
A person kept in custody.

normalIntro.en: A captive is someone a hand has closed around.
normalIntro.cn: captive 就是被一只手攥住的人。

normal.en: Capere means to seize.
normal.cn: capere 意为抓取。

normal.en: Captivus is the one seized.
normal.cn: captivus 就是被抓的人。

normal.en: A captive bird cannot leave.
normal.cn: 被关的鸟走不掉。

normal.en: A captive audience cannot either.
normal.cn: 走不开的听众也一样。

normal.en: The cage can be a room or a market.
normal.cn: 笼子可以是一间房或一个市场。

abstract.en: A door that only opens from outside.
abstract.cn: 只能从外面打开的门。

abstract.en: Wings folded by circumstance.
abstract.cn: 被处境折起的翅膀。

abstract.en: Staying because leaving is not offered.
abstract.cn: 因为没人提供离开而留下。

examples.en: The captive was released after two years.
examples.cn: 那名俘虏两年后获释。

examples.en: Zoo animals are captive by definition.
examples.cn: 动物园里的动物按定义就是被圈养的。

examples.en: The outage held the whole city captive to the radio.
examples.cn: 停电让全城只能守着收音机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普提夫」——被人一提就带走，成了俘虏。

root: 拉丁 capere（抓取）→ captivus（俘虏）→ 被俘的；受制的

sensesIntro.en: The prisoner and the stuck audience are both held by something they did not choose.
sensesIntro.cn: 俘虏与走不开的听众都被自己没选择的东西困住了。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird on a perch that has stopped trying the bars
core.cn: 核心意象：栖木上不再试栏杆的鸟

branches.en: Soldiers marched inland.
branches.cn: 被押往内陆的士兵。

branches.en: A bird that stopped beating the bars.
branches.cn: 不再撞栏杆的鸟。

branches.en: A hall with the doors shut.
branches.cn: 门已关闭的大厅。

branches.en: A market with one supplier.
branches.cn: 只有一个供货方的市场。

branches.en: Held where the exit is not yours.
branches.cn: 困在出口不由你决定之处。

intro.en: Captive is the noun behind captivate and captivity; the list below covers seizing and confinement.
intro.cn: captive 是 captivate 与 captivity 背后的名词；下面列出「抓取、囚禁」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere is to seize, hostis is an enemy, and prehendere is to grasp.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 意为抓取，hostis 意为敌人，prehendere 意为握住。

latinEntries.exampleCN: captivus 产生 captive 与 captivity。
hostis 产生 hostile 与 host。
prehendere 产生 prison 与 apprehend。

definition_zh: n. 囚禁，被俘（状态）；（因疾病、境遇而）受困
definition_en: the state of being kept a prisoner; the state of being confined by illness or circumstance
core_image: 笼中十一年、从未张开过的翅膀
scene: 它在笼子里活了十一年，从没张开过翅膀。It spent eleven years in captivity without ever opening its wings.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：captivity 指被囚禁的状态；句意是它在笼中十一年，从未张开翅膀。

forms.label: 不可数名词（无屈折变化）

senses.title: Being held prisoner
senses.definition: the condition of being kept in a place and not allowed to leave
senses.definitionCN: 被关在某处不许离开的处境
senses.example: He wrote the book during his captivity.
senses.exampleCN: 他在被囚期间写成了这本书。
senses.why: From Latin captivitas, the state of a captivus, a prisoner.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 captivitas，即俘虏 captivus 的状态。

senses.title: Being confined by circumstance
senses.definition: a state of being trapped by illness, poverty or duty rather than by walls
senses.definitionCN: 被疾病、贫困或责任而非墙壁困住的状态
senses.example: Illness held her in a quiet captivity at home.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病让她安静地困在家里。
senses.why: The walled prison loosens into any condition that removes choice.
senses.whyCN: 有墙的牢狱松动为任何剥夺选择的处境。

intro.en: Captivity is the abstract noun of captive, from Latin captivitas.
intro.cn: captivity 是 captive 的抽象名词，源自拉丁语 captivitas。

items.en: Captivus means a prisoner.
items.cn: captivus 意为俘虏。

items.en: Captivitas means the state of a prisoner.
items.cn: captivitas 意为被俘状态。

items.en: English captivity names imprisonment.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语指囚禁。

items.en: Animals are described as born in captivity.
items.cn: 十七世纪博物学出现「圈养中出生」。

items.en: Captivity appears in rules on prisoners of war.
items.cn: 十九世纪战俘法规使用此词。

items.en: Captivity covers animals in cages.
items.cn: 现代多指圈养动物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the capt- root; the near-meaning group ranks loss of freedom from a locked cell to a binding tie.
note.cn: 形近组共享 capt- 词根；近义组把失去自由从牢房排到束缚。

entries.definition: Kept as a prisoner.
To catch and hold.
Something that is done.
The state of being kept in prison.
The state of being kept within limits.
The state of being kept in custody.
The state of being bound or enslaved.

normalIntro.en: Captivity is the long version of being caught: not a moment, but years.
normalIntro.cn: captivity 是「被抓」的拉长版：不是一瞬，而是多年。

normal.en: Captive is the person.
normal.cn: captive 是人。

normal.en: Captivity is the state.
normal.cn: captivity 是状态。

normal.en: -ity turns adjectives into conditions.
normal.cn: -ity 把形容词变成状态名词。

normal.en: A caged bird lives in captivity.
normal.cn: 笼中鸟生活在被囚状态。

normal.en: Illness can do it without a cage.
normal.cn: 疾病不用笼子也能做到。

abstract.en: Time measured by a locked door.
abstract.cn: 用一扇锁着的门来计量的时间。

abstract.en: A life that asks permission from others.
abstract.cn: 事事要向别人请示的生活。

abstract.en: A condition long enough to become a home.
abstract.cn: 长到足以变成「家」的处境。

examples.en: The bird was bred in captivity.
examples.cn: 这只鸟是在圈养中繁殖的。

examples.en: His captivity lasted almost four years.
examples.cn: 他被囚禁将近四年。

examples.en: She described her captivity with great calm.
examples.cn: 她非常平静地讲述自己的被囚经历。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普提维提」——被人提来提去，哪也去不了，就是囚禁。

root: 拉丁 captivus（俘虏）+ -itas（状态）→ 被俘状态

sensesIntro.en: A cage and a sickroom can impose the same condition: the person cannot choose where to be.
sensesIntro.cn: 笼子与病房能造成同一种处境：这个人无法选择自己在哪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eleven years on a perch, wings never opened
core.cn: 核心意象：栖木上十一年、翅膀从未张开的鸟

branches.en: Years counted behind a locked door.
branches.cn: 在锁着的门后数过的年。

branches.en: A book written in prison.
branches.cn: 在狱中写成的书。

branches.en: A room made small by illness.
branches.cn: 被疾病缩小的一间房。

branches.en: A life limited by duty.
branches.cn: 被责任限制住的生活。

branches.en: Freedom removed without notice.
branches.cn: 未经通知就被拿走的自由。

intro.en: Captivity is captive plus -ity; the list below covers that abstract-noun suffix and the vocabulary of freedom lost.
intro.cn: captivity 是 captive 加 -ity；下面列出该抽象名词后缀以及「失去自由」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin captivitas is the state of a prisoner, vinculum is a bond, and finis is a boundary.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 captivitas 意为被俘状态，vinculum 意为锁链，finis 意为边界。

latinEntries.exampleCN: captivitas 产生 captivity。
vinculum 产生 bondage 与 vinculum。
finis 产生 confine 与 final。

definition_zh: 俘获；捕获；夺得；捕捉
definition_en: to catch a person or animal, or to take control of a place by force
core_image: 伸手把正在奔跑的东西一把抓住
scene: 警察当天就抓获了那名小偷。The police captured the thief the same day.
sceneCN: 这里 captured 是 capture 的过去式，意为「抓获」（第 1 个义项：把人或动物抓住）；句意是警察当天就抓住了那名小偷。

derivatives.zh: 与 capture 同根，义为「被俘虏的；被关起来的」
captive 加 -ity 构成，义为「囚禁状态」
由同一词根加 -or 构成，义为「捕获者、抓人的人」

senses.title: To catch a person or animal
senses.definition: to take a person or animal prisoner by force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力把人或动物抓住并控制住
senses.example: Soldiers captured three scouts near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵在河边抓获了三名侦察兵。
senses.why: Latin capere means to seize, and capture keeps that physical action of grabbing hold.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capere 意为「抓住」，capture 保留了抓住东西这一身体动作。

senses.title: To take control of a place
senses.definition: to seize a place or thing by force, especially in war
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指在战争中用武力夺取一个地方或物品
senses.example: The army captured the city after a long siege.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长期围困，军队攻占了这座城市。
senses.why: Taking a city is the same gesture as taking a prisoner, only the object is larger.
senses.whyCN: 攻下一座城与抓住一个人是同一个动作，只是对象变大了。

senses.title: To record or hold attention
senses.definition: to record an image, sound, or feeling, or to hold someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 把影像、声音或感受记录下来，或牢牢吸引住某人的注意
senses.example: The photograph captures the light of that morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这张照片捕捉到了那个早晨的光。
senses.why: A camera takes hold of a moment the way a hand takes hold of an object.
senses.whyCN: 相机「抓住」一个瞬间，正如手抓住一件物品，于是有了「捕捉影像」的义项。

intro.en: Capture comes straight from the Latin verb for seizing, by way of a noun meaning a taking.
intro.cn: capture 直接来自拉丁语中表示「抓取」的动词，经由一个意为「拿取」的名词进入英语。

items.en: capere meant to take, seize, or hold, and it is the root behind cap- and capt-.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、抓、控制」，是 cap- 与 capt- 词根的来源。

items.en: captura named a taking or a catch, especially of animals.
items.cn: captura 指「拿取、捕获」，尤其指猎获动物。

items.en: Old French capture kept the legal and military sense of taking a person or place.
items.cn: 古法语 capture 保留了夺取人或地方的法律与军事含义。

items.en: English borrowed capture for the act of taking a prisoner or a town.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 capture，指俘获俘虏或攻占城镇。

items.en: Photography and computing extended it to recording images, sound, and data.
items.cn: 摄影与计算机技术把它的词义扩展到记录影像、声音和数据。

note.en: Capture belongs to the Latin family of seizing, and its near meanings all involve taking hold.
note.cn: capture 属于拉丁语「抓取」词族，近义词都与「抓住」有关。

entries.definition: kept as a prisoner
entries.definitionCN: 被俘虏的、被关押的，与 capture 同根。

entries.definition: a person who captures someone
entries.definitionCN: 捕获者、抓人的人，由同一词根加 -or 构成。

entries.definition: to hold someone's attention completely
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷，字面意思是「把人抓住」。

entries.definition: to take hold of something suddenly and by force
entries.definitionCN: 突然用力抓住某物，最贴近 capture 的动作义。

entries.definition: to take someone into legal custody
entries.definitionCN: 依法逮捕某人，对应「抓获」义。

entries.definition: to take something quickly and roughly
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而粗鲁地抓住，是口语说法。

normalIntro.en: The root capt- means seized, and every sense is a version of taking hold.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 capt- 意为「被抓住」，每个义项都是「抓住」的一种版本。

normal.en: capt- comes from Latin capere, to seize, the same root as captive and captor.
normal.cn: capt- 来自拉丁语 capere（抓取），与 captive、captor 同根。

normal.en: A prisoner is captured, and so is a city: the verb does not change.
normal.cn: 俘虏可以被 capture，城市也可以被 capture，动词本身不变。

normal.en: capture the attention treats attention as something that can be grabbed.
normal.cn: capture the attention 把注意力当成可以抓走的东西。

normal.en: A camera captures a moment, which links photography with the same old verb.
normal.cn: 相机 capture 一个瞬间，把摄影和这个古老动词连在一起。

normal.en: The noun capture is simply the act: the capture of the town.
normal.cn: 名词 capture 就是那个动作本身：攻占该镇。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around a bird that was about to fly away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手合拢，抓住一只正要飞走的鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a flag being pulled down and another raised in its place.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗被拉下，另一面旗在原地升起。

abstract.en: Picture a camera shutter closing on one second of light.
abstract.cn: 想象相机快门合拢，把一秒的光收进去。

examples.en: The police captured the thief the same day.
examples.cn: 警察当天就抓获了那名小偷。

examples.en: The army captured the city after a long siege.
examples.cn: 经过长期围困，军队攻占了这座城市。

examples.en: The photograph captures the light of that morning.
examples.cn: 这张照片捕捉到了那个早晨的光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普车」——开车追上去，一把把人抓住。

root: 拉丁语 capere（抓住、夺取）→ captura（捕获）→ 古法语 capture → 英语 capture。

sensesIntro.en: One gesture of seizing runs through all senses, from prisoners to cities to photographs.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「抓住」的动作贯穿全部义项，从俘虏到城市再到照片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing around something that is trying to get away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢，抓住正想逃走的东西。

branches.en: The personal sense: taking a person or animal prisoner.
branches.cn: 指人的义项：把人或动物抓为俘虏。

branches.en: The territorial sense: taking a city or position by force.
branches.cn: 指地域的义项：用武力攻占城市或阵地。

branches.en: The recording sense: taking an image, sound, or feeling into a device.
branches.cn: 记录义：把影像、声音或感受收进设备里。

branches.en: Both older senses share the idea of force against a resisting object.
branches.cn: 两个较早的义项都共享「以武力对付抵抗者」的意思。

branches.en: The modern sense softens force into attention: a good story captures listeners.
branches.cn: 现代义把「武力」软化为「吸引力」：好故事能抓住听众。

intro.en: Capture is built on the root capt-, seized, with the noun and verb ending -ure.
intro.cn: capture 建立在词根 capt-（被抓住的）上，加上名词兼动词词尾 -ure。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere and captura give English capture, captive, and captor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 与 captura 给英语带来 capture、captive、captor 等词。

items.example: They captured the moment on film.
items.exampleCN: 他们用胶片记录下那个瞬间。

items.meaning: he, she, or it seizes something
items.example: The novel captures village life well.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说很好地捕捉了乡村生活。

items.meaning: seized or recorded in the past
items.example: The rebels captured the radio station.

items.meaning: the act of seizing or recording
items.example: The team is capturing images of the coast.
items.exampleCN: 团队正在拍摄海岸影像。

items.example: The captive birds were later released.
items.exampleCN: 被关的鸟后来被放生了。

items.meaning: the state of being held prisoner
items.example: The animal was born in captivity.
items.exampleCN: 这只动物出生在圈养环境中。

items.example: The captor released the driver unharmed.
items.exampleCN: 劫持者未伤司机便将其释放。
capere 是整个词族的底层词根。

definition_zh: 碳；复写纸
definition_en: a chemical element found in coal, diamonds, and all living things
core_image: 烧成黑色的木炭，仍保留着火的痕迹
scene: 钻石和石墨都由碳构成。Both diamond and graphite are made of carbon.
sceneCN: 这里 carbon 是「碳」（第 1 个义项：一种化学元素）；句意是钻石和石墨这两种外观完全不同的物质都由碳构成。

derivatives.zh: carbon 加 -ate 构成，义为「碳酸盐」
carbon 加 -ic 构成，义为「碳酸的」
carbon 加 -ize 构成，义为「使碳化」

senses.title: The chemical element of coal and diamonds
senses.definition: a chemical element that forms coal, diamonds, and the bodies of living things
senses.definitionCN: 构成煤、钻石和生物体的一种化学元素
senses.example: Carbon is the basic building block of all living things.
senses.exampleCN: 碳是一切生物的基本组成单元。
senses.why: Latin carbo meant charcoal or a glowing coal, the visible form of this element.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 carbo 指木炭或烧红的炭，正是这种元素最直观的形态。

senses.title: Thin paper that copies writing
senses.definition: thin dark paper placed under a sheet so that writing passes through
senses.definitionCN: 垫在纸下、让字迹透过去的深色薄纸
senses.example: The receipt was typed with carbon paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那张收据是用复写纸打出来的。
senses.why: The black coating on such paper is made of carbon, so the paper took the element's name.
senses.whyCN: 这种纸上的黑色涂层由碳制成，于是纸张直接借用了元素的名字。

intro.en: Carbon is an old charcoal word that chemistry gave a precise new meaning.
intro.cn: carbon 是一个古老的「木炭」词，化学给了它精确的新含义。

items.en: carbo meant a piece of charcoal or a glowing coal.
items.cn: carbo 指一块木炭或烧红的炭。

items.en: French chemists used carbone for the element they had isolated from charcoal.
items.cn: 法国化学家用 carbone 称呼他们从木炭中分离出的元素。

items.en: English borrowed carbone as carbon during the chemical revolution.
items.cn: 在化学革命期间，英语借入 carbone，写作 carbon。

items.en: The word spread into compounds such as carbon dioxide and carbon paper.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到二氧化碳、复写纸等复合词中。

items.en: Today carbon is central to climate talk, as in carbon footprint and carbon emissions.
items.cn: 今天 carbon 是气候话题的核心词，如碳足迹与碳排放。

note.en: Carbon has a large chemical family, and it is also the name of several very different materials.
note.cn: carbon 有一个庞大的化学词族，同时也指几种外观差别很大的材料。

entries.definition: a salt containing carbon and oxygen
entries.definitionCN: 含碳和氧的盐类，由 carbon 加 -ate 构成。

entries.definition: relating to carbon, especially in acids
entries.definitionCN: 与碳有关的，尤指碳酸的。

entries.definition: to turn something into carbon or charcoal
black material made by burning wood slowly
entries.definitionCN: 木材慢烧制成的黑色材料，与 carbon 的古义最接近。

entries.definition: a soft black form of carbon used in pencils
entries.definitionCN: 石墨，一种柔软的黑色碳单质，用于铅笔芯。

entries.definition: a very hard clear form of carbon
entries.definitionCN: 钻石，碳的一种极硬透明形态。

normalIntro.en: The element hides inside the old word for charcoal, and the family shows its many forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个元素躲在古老的「木炭」词里，而词族展示了它的多种形态。

normal.en: carbon comes from Latin carbo, charcoal, so the word is older than chemistry.
normal.cn: carbon 来自拉丁语 carbo（木炭），这个词比化学更古老。

normal.en: carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide name gases built on carbon.
normal.cn: carbon dioxide 与 carbon monoxide 都是以碳为基础的气体名称。

normal.en: carbon paper copies writing because its black layer is carbon.
normal.cn: 复写纸能复印字迹，是因为它的黑色涂层就是碳。

normal.en: carbon footprint measures the carbon a person or product leaves behind.
normal.cn: 碳足迹衡量一个人或一件产品留下的碳排放。

normal.en: Carbon is uncountable, so it takes no plural in ordinary use.
normal.cn: carbon 作元素名时不可数，日常使用没有复数。

abstract.en: Picture a blackened stick pulled from a fire, still warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一根从火里抽出的黑木棍，还带着余温。

abstract.en: Picture the same element as dull pencil lead and as a brilliant diamond.
abstract.cn: 想象同一种元素，一面是暗灰的铅笔芯，一面是璀璨的钻石。

abstract.en: Picture a dark layer under a sheet of paper catching every stroke of the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象纸下那层黑色材料，接住笔尖的每一次划动。

examples.en: Both diamond and graphite are made of carbon.
examples.cn: 钻石和石墨都由碳构成。

examples.en: Carbon is the basic building block of all living things.
examples.cn: 碳是一切生物的基本组成单元。

examples.en: The receipt was typed with carbon paper.
examples.cn: 那张收据是用复写纸打出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡本」——烧成炭的木本，剩下的黑色就是碳。

root: 拉丁语 carbo（木炭、炭火）→ 法语 carbone → 英语 carbon；同根词有 charcoal、carbonic。

sensesIntro.en: One element appears as charcoal, as diamond, and as the black layer of copying paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种元素，既以木炭出现，也以钻石出现，还以复写纸的黑色涂层出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: black charcoal left after fire, the visible trace of one element.
core.cn: 核心意象：火熄灭后留下的黑炭，是一种元素可见的痕迹。

branches.en: The chemical sense: the element shared by coal, diamonds, and living tissue.
branches.cn: 化学义：煤、钻石与生物组织共有的元素。

branches.en: The office sense: dark paper that transfers writing.
branches.cn: 办公义：能转印字迹的深色纸张。

branches.en: Compounds such as carbon dioxide and carbon fibre are built on the element.
branches.cn: 二氧化碳、碳纤维等复合词都以这一元素为基础。

branches.en: Climate language turns the element into a measure of human impact.
branches.cn: 气候话题把这一元素变成了衡量人类影响的指标。

branches.en: The copying sense survives mainly in carbon paper and carbon copy.
branches.cn: 复写义主要保留在复写纸与副本这两个说法里。

intro.en: Carbon is a base noun from Latin, and chemistry built a large family on it.
intro.cn: carbon 是来自拉丁语的基础名词，化学在它之上建起了一个大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin carbo, charcoal, is the source of carbon and of several chemical terms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carbo（木炭）是 carbon 及若干化学术语的来源。

items.meaning: the element found in coal and diamonds
items.meaningCN: 碳，存在于煤和钻石中的元素
items.example: Carbon has six protons in each atom.
items.exampleCN: 每个碳原子有六个质子。

items.example: The rock is mostly calcium carbonate.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石主要是碳酸钙。

items.example: Carbonic acid forms when gas dissolves in water.
items.exampleCN: 气体溶于水时形成碳酸。

items.example: The heat carbonized the outer layer of wood.

items.meaningCN: 含二氧化碳的，指碳酸饮料

items.example: The city plans to decarbonize its buses.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市计划让公交车脱碳。

items.meaning: black material made by burning wood

definition_zh: adj. 最重要的，基本的；n. 红衣主教；（北美）红雀
definition_en: most important or fundamental; a senior bishop of the Roman Catholic Church; a red songbird
core_image: 一扇门的铰链：一切都绕着它转，一切都靠它支撑
scene: 规则有四条，第一条最要紧：先确认，再动手。The cardinal rule was to check before acting.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：cardinal 指最重要的；句意是首要规则是先确认再动手。

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: of the greatest importance, the thing everything else depends on
senses.definitionCN: 最重要的、其他一切所依赖的东西
senses.example: Accuracy is the cardinal rule in this lab.
senses.exampleCN: 准确是本实验室的首要规则。
senses.why: Latin cardinalis means a hinge, and a hinge is what a door turns on.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cardinalis 意为铰链，而门正绕铰链转动。

senses.title: A senior bishop
senses.definition: a senior official of the Roman Catholic Church who advises the pope
senses.definitionCN: 罗马天主教会中协助教皇的高级神职人员
senses.example: The cardinals met to choose a new pope.
senses.exampleCN: 红衣主教们聚集推选新教皇。
senses.why: Church offices were seen as hinges of the church, and the name stuck.
senses.whyCN: 教会职位被视为教会的「铰链」，名称沿用下来。

senses.title: The red songbird
senses.definition: a North American finch with bright red plumage in the male
senses.definitionCN: 雄鸟羽色鲜红的北美雀类
senses.example: A cardinal sat on the fence in the snow.
senses.exampleCN: 一只红雀停在雪中的栅栏上。
senses.why: The bird was named for the red robes of the church officers.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟因红衣主教的红色长袍而得名。

intro.en: Cardinal comes from Latin cardo, a hinge, the part everything turns on.
intro.cn: cardinal 源自拉丁语 cardo（铰链），即一切所绕其转动的部件。

items.en: Cardo means a hinge.
items.cn: cardo 意为铰链。

items.en: Cardinalis means relating to a hinge, hence principal.
items.cn: cardinalis 意为铰链的，因而指主要的。

items.en: Senior clergy are called cardinals.
items.cn: 十二世纪高级神职人员被称为红衣主教。

items.en: English cardinal means chief or fundamental.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语意为首要的、基本的。

items.en: The red bird is named for the red robes.
items.cn: 十七世纪红雀因红袍得名。

items.en: Cardinal covers rules, numbers and birds.
items.cn: 现代涵盖规则、基数与红雀。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the card- opening; the near-meaning group ranks importance from principal to outright essential.
note.cn: 形近组共享 card- 开头；近义组把重要性从首要排到必不可少。

entries.definition: A festival with music and parades.
The study of the heart.
A piece of stiff paper or plastic.
The number of members in a set.
Most important or main.
The most important or highest.
Forming the base of something.
Absolutely necessary.

normalIntro.en: A cardinal rule is a hinge: everything else swings on it.
normalIntro.cn: 首要规则就是铰链：别的都绕着它转。

normal.en: Cardo means hinge.
normal.cn: cardo 意为铰链。

normal.en: Cardinal means turning on a hinge.
normal.cn: cardinal 意为绕着铰链转。

normal.en: So a cardinal rule holds everything else.
normal.cn: 所以首要规则支撑其余一切。

normal.en: Church cardinals were hinges of the church.
normal.cn: 红衣主教是教会的「铰链」。

normal.en: The red bird took their colour.
normal.cn: 红雀借了他们的颜色。

abstract.en: The point a door cannot do without.
abstract.cn: 门不可或缺的那个点。

abstract.en: One rule the rest are built on.
abstract.cn: 其余规则都建在其上的一条规则。

abstract.en: Red robes and a red bird.
abstract.cn: 红袍与一只红鸟。

examples.en: Safety is the cardinal rule on the site.
examples.cn: 安全是工地的首要规则。

examples.en: The cardinals gathered in Rome.
examples.cn: 红衣主教们在罗马集会。

examples.en: A male cardinal flashed red against the hedge.
examples.cn: 一只雄红雀在树篱前闪过一片红。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡的诺」——所有规矩都「卡」在这一点上，最关键。

root: 拉丁 cardo（铰链）+ -alis（……的）→ 像铰链一样关键的

sensesIntro.en: A hinge, a senior churchman and a red bird all meet in one word because each has been treated as the thing everything turns on, or the colour of those who were.
sensesIntro.cn: 铰链、高级神职者与红鸟汇于一词：前者是一切的支点，后者借了那些人的颜色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hinge that every swing of the door depends on
core.cn: 核心意象：门的每一次开合都依赖的那个铰链

branches.en: A rule nothing may break.
branches.cn: 任何情况都不许破的规则。

branches.en: The four main compass points.
branches.cn: 四个基本方位。

branches.en: Bishops in red in Rome.
branches.cn: 罗马穿红衣的主教们。

branches.en: A red bird on a snowy fence.
branches.cn: 雪中栅栏上的红鸟。

branches.en: The church hinge and its colour.
branches.cn: 教会的「铰链」与它的颜色。

intro.en: Cardinal is cardo plus -alis; the list below covers that hinge-root and the vocabulary of rank and importance.
intro.cn: cardinal 是 cardo 加 -alis；下面列出该铰链词根以及「等级、重要性」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cardo is a hinge, principium is a beginning, and fundus is a base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cardo 意为铰链，principium 意为开端，fundus 意为基底。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cardo 产生 cardinal。
principium 产生 principal 与 principle。
fundus 产生 fund 与 foundation。

definition_zh: 心血管的；心血管系统的
definition_en: relating to the heart and the blood vessels, especially as a single system
core_image: 一颗心脏连着动脉与静脉网络，构成一套封闭的输送系统
scene: 常年跑步让他的心血管比同龄人更有力。Regular exercise lowers the risk of cardiovascular disease.
sceneCN: 这里 cardiovascular 指「心血管的」（第 1 个义项：同时涉及心脏与血管）；句意：规律运动降低心血管疾病的风险。图中可辨识物件：心脏、冠状动脉、动脉树、跑步鞋。

pos.zh: 心血管的；心血管系统的（同时涉及心脏与血管）

collocations.zh: 心血管事件（如心梗、中风）

senses.title: Heart and vessels together
senses.titleCN: 心血管的：同时涉及心脏与血管
senses.definition: relating to the heart and the blood vessels considered as one system
senses.definitionCN: 指同时涉及作为单一系统的心脏与血管
senses.example: Regular exercise lowers the risk of cardiovascular disease.
senses.exampleCN: 规律运动降低心血管疾病的风险。
senses.why: The word joins Greek kardia 'heart' to Latin vasculum 'small vessel', naming the two halves of one loop.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊 kardia「心脏」与拉丁 vasculum「小血管」连接起来，命名同一个环的两半。

senses.title: The cardiovascular system
senses.titleCN: 心血管系统：泵与管道构成的整体
senses.definition: the heart, arteries, veins and capillaries taken as a single transport system
senses.definitionCN: 把心脏、动脉、静脉与毛细血管视为一套输送系统
senses.example: The cardiovascular system is closed in mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 哺乳动物的心血管系统是闭合的。
senses.why: Medicine prefers one adjective for the pump-and-pipe unit, because diseases rarely respect the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 医学偏爱用一个形容词指「泵加管道」的整体，因为疾病很少尊重这条分界。

senses.title: Cardiovascular disease
senses.titleCN: 心血管疾病：心梗、中风、高血压等
senses.definition: the group of disorders of the heart and vessels, including heart attack, stroke and hypertension
senses.definitionCN: 心脏与血管疾病的总称，包括心梗、中风与高血压
senses.example: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death globally.
senses.exampleCN: 心血管疾病仍是全球首要死因。
senses.why: Epidemiology needed a single label to group conditions that share risk factors and prevention.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学需要一个统一标签，把共享危险因素与预防手段的病症归为一组。

senses.title: Cardiovascular health
senses.titleCN: 心血管健康：系统的功能状态
senses.definition: the general condition of the heart and vessels, measured by pressure, lipids and fitness
senses.definitionCN: 心脏与血管的整体状况，由血压、血脂与体能衡量
senses.example: Diet and sleep both shape cardiovascular health.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食与睡眠都影响心血管健康。
senses.why: Prevention language needed a positive label, so the adjective came to name the state to be protected, not only the disease to be avoided.
senses.whyCN: 预防语汇需要一个正面标签，于是这个形容词开始命名需要被保护的状态，而不只是要避免的疾病。

senses.title: Cardiovascular fitness
senses.titleCN: 心血管适能：持续运动的能力
senses.definition: the ability of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen during sustained exercise
senses.definitionCN: 心脏与肺在持续运动中供应氧气的能力
senses.example: Running builds cardiovascular fitness faster than walking.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步比走路更快提升心血管适能。
senses.why: Sports science borrowed the medical adjective for the endurance side of training, later shortened to cardio.
senses.whyCN: 运动科学借用了医学形容词指训练的耐力面，后来缩略为 cardio。

senses.title: Cardiovascular risk
senses.titleCN: 心血管风险：发生事件的概率
senses.definition: the estimated probability of a heart attack, stroke or other vascular event
senses.definitionCN: 发生心梗、中风或其他血管事件的估计概率
senses.example: Smoking doubles cardiovascular risk in young adults.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟使年轻人的心血管风险翻倍。
senses.why: Risk turns the system into a probability, estimated from pressure, lipids and smoking rather than observed directly.
senses.whyCN: 风险把系统变成一个概率，它由血压、血脂与吸烟估算而来，而非直接观察。

senses.title: Cardiovascular event
senses.titleCN: 心血管事件：突发的临床发作
senses.definition: a sudden clinical occurrence such as a heart attack or stroke
senses.definitionCN: 突发的临床发作，如心肌梗死或中风
senses.example: The trial counted every cardiovascular event over five years.
senses.exampleCN: 该试验统计了五年内每一次心血管事件。
senses.why: Trials count discrete occurrences, so the adjective attaches to 'event' as the unit of outcome.
senses.whyCN: 试验统计的是一次次离散的发生，因此这个形容词附着在 event 上，作为结局的单位。

senses.title: Cardiovascular drugs and surgery
senses.definition: describes treatments aimed at the heart and vessels, such as stents or blood-pressure drugs
senses.definitionCN: 形容针对心脏与血管的治疗，如支架或降压药
senses.example: Cardiovascular surgery replaced two blocked arteries.
senses.exampleCN: 心血管手术替换了两条堵塞的动脉。
senses.why: Treatment language attaches the adjective to what is done to the pump and pipes, not to what they are.
senses.whyCN: 治疗语汇把这个形容词附着在「对泵与管道做了什么」上，而不是它们本身是什么。

intro.en: Cardiovascular is a hybrid compound: Greek kardia 'heart' plus Latin vasculum 'small vessel', joined by the combining vowel -o-. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: cardiovascular 是混合复合词：希腊 kardia「心脏」加拉丁 vasculum「小血管」，由连接元音 -o- 结合。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Kardia meant 'heart' both as an organ and as the seat of feeling. It gives English cardiac, cardiology and the prefix cardio-.
items.cn: kardia 既指作为器官的心脏，也指情感的所在。它产生英语 cardiac、cardiology 与前缀 cardio-。

items.en: Vas meant 'vessel, container'; its diminutive vasculum meant 'small vessel', and vascularis gave English vascular.
items.cn: vas 意为「容器、器皿」；其指小形式 vasculum 意为「小容器」，vascularis 给出英语 vascular。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine often joined a Greek prefix to a Latin stem, because both languages already supplied the technical vocabulary.
items.cn: 19 世纪医学常把希腊前缀与拉丁词干拼接，因为两种语言都已提供了专业词汇。

items.en: Cardiovascular is recorded in the late nineteenth century, around the 1870s. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: cardiovascular 记录于 19 世纪后期，约在 1870 年代。最早的确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Twentieth-century epidemiology made cardiovascular disease a standard category and later shortened the fitness sense to cardio.
items.cn: 20 世纪流行病学使 cardiovascular disease 成为标准类别，后来又把体能义缩略为 cardio。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact date of the coinage is uncertain, and the deeper origins of both kardia and vas are reconstructions rather than recorded words.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：该词的确切造词年代存疑；kardia 与 vas 的更深来源均属重构形式，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words that name one half of the compound or a neighbour; the second holds near-synonyms for the same system and its health.
note.cn: 第一组是指称复合词某一半或相邻概念的词；第二组是「同一系统及其健康」的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating only to the heart, as in cardiac arrest; cardiovascular also covers the vessels.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指心脏，如心脏停搏；cardiovascular 还包括血管。

entries.definition: Relating only to blood vessels; it omits the pump.
Informal shorthand for cardiovascular exercise, not for the medical adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中是有氧运动的简称，不是医学形容词的替代。

entries.definition: The branch of medicine dealing with the heart; the adjective describes patients and risks, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究心脏的医学分支；形容词描述病人与风险，不指学科。

entries.definition: Relating to the whole blood circuit, including the blood itself; cardiovascular stresses heart and vessels.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个血液环路，包括血液本身；cardiovascular 强调心脏与血管。

entries.definition: Relating to the arteries that supply the heart muscle; it is narrower than cardiovascular.
entries.definitionCN: 指供应心肌的动脉，比 cardiovascular 范围窄。

entries.definition: Relating to the heart and lungs, a pairing used for resuscitation and fitness testing.
entries.definitionCN: 指心脏与肺，用于复苏与体能测试。

entries.definition: Relating to hardening and plaque in arteries, one mechanism within cardiovascular disease.
entries.definitionCN: 指动脉硬化与斑块形成，是心血管疾病中的一种机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cardio- 'heart' + vascular 'vessels': the pump and the pipes named together.
normal.cn: cardio-「心脏」+ vascular「血管」：泵与管道一起命名。

normal.en: The family runs cardiac, cardiology, cardiologist, vascular and cardiopulmonary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cardiac、cardiology、cardiologist、vascular、cardiopulmonary。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: cardiovascular disease, cardiovascular risk, cardiovascular event.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：心血管疾病、心血管风险、心血管事件。

normal.en: The gym word cardio is a shortening of cardiovascular exercise.
normal.cn: 健身房里的 cardio 是 cardiovascular exercise 的缩略。

normal.en: cardiac is only the heart; vascular is only the vessels.
normal.cn: cardiac 只指心脏，vascular 只指血管。

abstract.en: Picture a pump with red and blue pipes branching through a whole body.
abstract.cn: 想象一台泵，红色与蓝色管道布满全身。

abstract.en: Picture a treadmill readout showing heart rate and oxygen use together.
abstract.cn: 想象跑步机的读数同时显示心率与耗氧量。

abstract.en: Picture a plaque narrowing a coronary artery like sediment in a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象斑块像管道里的沉积物一样把冠状动脉收窄。

examples.en: Cardiovascular disease accounts for about a third of deaths worldwide.
examples.cn: 心血管疾病约占全球死亡人数的三分之一。

examples.en: Thirty minutes of cardiovascular exercise five times a week is a common target.
examples.cn: 每周五次、每次三十分钟的有氧运动是常见目标。

examples.en: The study tracked cardiovascular events over ten years.
examples.cn: 该研究追踪了十年间的心血管事件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cardio 心 + vascular 血管」——心脏加血管 → cardiovascular 心血管的

root: 希腊 kardia「心脏」+ 拉丁 vasculum「小血管」→ 19 世纪医学混合复合词 cardiovascular。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one system: the heart and its pipes can be named together, then measured as health, fitness, risk, event, and finally as a target of drugs and surgery.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个系统展开：心脏与管道可以一起命名，随后被衡量为健康、适能、风险、事件，最后成为药物与手术的靶点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pump and a branching network of pipes serving one closed loop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台泵与一套分叉管道，服务同一个闭合环路。

branches.en: THE UNIT: the compound exists to name heart and vessels as one thing.
branches.cn: 整体单元：这个复合词的存在，就是把心脏与血管命名为一件事。

branches.en: THE CLINICAL FACE: disease is the negative measure of the same system's health.
branches.cn: 临床面孔：疾病是同一系统健康的反向度量。

branches.en: THE TRAINING FACE: fitness asks how much oxygen the system can deliver under load.
branches.cn: 训练面孔：适能问的是系统在负荷下能输送多少氧气。

branches.en: PROBABILITY AND EVENT: risk is the forecast, an event is the occurrence.
branches.cn: 概率与事件：风险是预测，事件是实际发生。

branches.en: THE TARGET: drugs and surgery address the same pump and pipes.
branches.cn: 靶点：药物与手术处理的仍是同一台泵与同一套管道。

intro.en: Cardiovascular is a Greek heart stem plus a Latin vessel adjective, a hybrid typical of scientific English.
intro.cn: cardiovascular 是希腊「心脏」词干加拉丁「血管」形容词，是科学英语常见的混合构造。

latinIntro.en: Greek kardia supplies cardiac, cardiology and cardio-; Latin vas and vasculum supply vascular and vasculature.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 kardia 提供 cardiac、cardiology 与 cardio-；拉丁 vas 与 vasculum 提供 vascular 与 vasculature。

items.meaning: relating to the heart and vessels
items.example: Cardiovascular health depends on blood pressure.
items.exampleCN: 心血管健康取决于血压。

items.example: She trained in cardiology for four years.
items.exampleCN: 她接受了四年心脏病学训练。
心脏科医生安排了血管造影。

items.example: Vascular tissue carries water in plants.
items.exampleCN: 维管组织在植物中输送水分。

items.meaning: the vessel network of an organ
items.example: The tumour has a dense vasculature.
items.exampleCN: 这个肿瘤血管网络密集。

items.example: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation restores breathing and circulation.
items.exampleCN: 心肺复苏恢复呼吸与循环。

items.meaningCN: 健身语境中的有氧运动
items.example: She does forty minutes of cardio daily.
items.exampleCN: 她每天做四十分钟有氧运动。

definition_zh: 职业；生涯
definition_en: the job or series of jobs that a person does over a long period of life
core_image: 一条越跑越宽的跑道，人一直在上面往前
scene: 她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。She began her career in journalism.
sceneCN: 这里 career 是「职业生涯」（第 1 个义项：长期从事的工作历程）；句意是她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。

derivatives.zh: career 加 -ist 构成，义为「一味追求升迁的人」
career 加 -ism 构成，义为「追逐个人事业成功」

senses.title: The work a person does over years
senses.definition: the profession or occupation that a person follows for much of their life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人一生中大部分时间从事的专业或工作
senses.example: Teaching became his career after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后教书成了他的职业。
senses.why: Career first meant a racecourse, and a working life came to be seen as a course run over years.
senses.whyCN: career 最初指跑道，而人的工作历程被看成一条跑过多年的赛道。

senses.title: The whole course of working life
senses.definition: the whole period of a person's working life, with its progress and changes
senses.definitionCN: 一个人工作生活的整个时期，包括其中的进展与变化
senses.example: Her career spanned three decades and two continents.
senses.exampleCN: 她的生涯横跨三十年、两个大洲。
senses.why: A course has a start and a finish, so career also names the full span rather than one job.
senses.whyCN: 跑道有起点和终点，所以 career 也指整段历程，而不只是某一份工作。

intro.en: Career began as a word for a racetrack, then became the track of a working life.
intro.cn: career 起初指赛马跑道，后来变成「工作人生的跑道」。

items.en: carrus named a wheeled wagon, the source of many words about vehicles and tracks.
items.cn: carrus 指带轮的车，是许多车辆与道路词的来源。

items.en: carriere meant a racecourse or the track on which horses ran.
items.cn: carriere 指赛马场或马匹奔跑的跑道。

items.en: English borrowed career for a racecourse and for a galloping course.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 career，指跑道与疾驰的路线。

items.en: The word shifted from a physical track to the course of a person's public life.
items.cn: 这个词从实体的跑道转指一个人公共生活的历程。

items.en: Today career means the profession itself and the whole span of working life.
items.cn: 今天 career 既指职业本身，也指整个工作生涯。

note.en: Career is a descendant of the wagon word car, and it sits beside other names for work.
note.cn: career 是「马车」一词 car 的后代，同时和别的「工作」名称相邻。

entries.definition: a road vehicle with an engine
entries.definitionCN: 汽车，与 career 同出拉丁语 carrus。

entries.definition: a railway car or a horse-drawn vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 火车车厢或马车，与 career 同根。

entries.definition: a two-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses in ancient races
entries.definitionCN: 古代赛车上用的双轮马车，同样源自 carrus。

entries.definition: a job requiring special training
entries.definitionCN: 需要专门训练的职业，最贴近 career 的第一义。

entries.definition: the kind of work a person does
entries.definitionCN: 一个人所从事的工作类别，较正式的用词。

entries.definition: a particular paid position
entries.definitionCN: 一份具体的有薪职位，时间跨度比 career 短。

normalIntro.en: The racetrack image makes the word easy: a career is the course you run for years.
normalIntro.cn: 跑道的画面让这个词很好记：career 就是你跑了很多年的那条赛道。

normal.en: career comes from carriere, a racecourse, built on the wagon word carrus.
normal.cn: career 来自 carriere（跑道），建立在「马车」一词 carrus 之上。

normal.en: A racecourse has a start and a direction, just like a working life.
normal.cn: 跑道有起点和方向，工作人生也一样。

normal.en: career path and career choice both use the road metaphor directly.
normal.cn: career path 与 career choice 都直接沿用了「道路」这个比喻。

normal.en: The phrase launch a career treats work as a vehicle setting off.
normal.cn: launch a career 把事业看成一辆出发的车。

normal.en: The plural careers covers several people's working lives.
normal.cn: 复数 careers 指多人的职业生涯。

abstract.en: Picture a long track curving out of sight, with footprints already on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的跑道弯出视线，上面已有脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a horse cart on the same track, then a car, then a person walking.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条跑道上先是马车，再是汽车，最后是一个步行的人。

abstract.en: Picture a single line drawn through many years on a calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象在日历上画一条穿过许多年的线。

examples.en: She began her career in journalism.
examples.cn: 她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。

examples.en: Teaching became his career after graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业后教书成了他的职业。

examples.en: Her career spanned three decades and two continents.
examples.cn: 她的生涯横跨三十年、两个大洲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可瑞尔」——在跑道上一直往前跑，就是职业生涯。

root: 拉丁语 carrus（车）→ 古法语 carriere（跑道）→ 英语 career（跑道，后指人生历程）。

sensesIntro.en: One metaphor, two reaches: the profession itself and the whole course it runs on.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个比喻，两种跨度：职业本身，以及它所在的那整条跑道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a racetrack stretching forward, with someone running along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条向前延伸的跑道，有人正在上面奔跑。

branches.en: The job sense: the profession a person settles into.
branches.cn: 工作义：一个人长期从事的职业。

branches.en: The span sense: the whole run from first job to retirement.
branches.cn: 跨度义：从第一份工作到退休的整段历程。

branches.en: Both senses borrow the shape of a track: direction, progress, and distance covered.
branches.cn: 两个义项都借用了跑道的形状：方向、进展和已跑过的距离。

branches.en: career development treats the job as something that can be built stage by stage.
branches.cn: career development 把职业看成可以分阶段搭建的东西。

branches.en: A career can be long or short, smooth or broken, like any course.
branches.cn: 生涯可长可短、可顺可断，就像任何一条跑道。

intro.en: Career is a base noun; the suffix -ist and -ism build its small modern family.
intro.cn: career 是基础名词，后缀 -ist 与 -ism 构成它不大的现代词族。

latinIntro.en: The root goes back to Latin carrus, a wagon, which also gives car and carriage.
latinIntro.cn: 词根可追溯到拉丁语 carrus（车），它也带来 car 与 carriage。

items.example: The school advises students on careers.
items.exampleCN: 学校为学生提供职业指导。

items.meaning: a person who puts career success first
items.meaningCN: 一心追求事业升迁的人
items.example: He was seen as a careerist.
items.exampleCN: 他被看作一个只顾往上爬的人。

items.meaning: the pursuit of personal career success

items.example: Critics blamed careerism for the decision.
items.exampleCN: 批评者把这一决定归咎于追逐名利。

definition_zh: 食肉动物；肉食者；食虫植物
definition_en: an animal that feeds chiefly on the flesh of other animals, or a plant that traps and digests small animals
core_image: 一只狼低头撕咬猎物后腿，嘴边沾着血，雪地上留着拖行的痕迹
scene: 夜里留下的爪印属于一种大型食肉动物。The wolf is a social carnivore that brings down prey far larger than itself.
sceneCN: 这里 carnivore 指「食肉动物」（第 1 个义项：以动物肉为主要食物）；狼是群居食肉动物，能放倒比自己大得多的猎物。图中可辨识物件：狼、猎物、雪地拖痕、血迹。

pos.zh: 食肉动物；肉食者；食虫植物（可数，复数 carnivores）

collocations.zh: 专性食肉动物；必须吃肉才能存活
食肉动物集团；同一群落中共享猎物的食肉者集合
食虫植物（常用形容词形式）
人类的食肉者；以肉为主食的人

derivatives.zh: 裂齿的；食肉动物用于剪切肉类的牙齿
食肉目；哺乳动物中的一个目

senses.title: Flesh-eating animal
senses.titleCN: 食肉动物：以动物肉为主食
senses.definition: an animal whose diet consists mainly of the flesh of other animals
senses.definitionCN: 指以其他动物的肉为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Wolves are carnivores that hunt in packs.
senses.exampleCN: 狼是成群狩猎的食肉动物。
senses.why: The word names a dietary class by its food, so a carnivore is defined by what it eats rather than by how it kills.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按食物命名食性类别，因此食肉动物由吃什么界定，而不是由如何杀界定。

senses.title: Obligate carnivore
senses.titleCN: 专性食肉：无法靠植物维生
senses.definition: a carnivore that cannot survive on plant food alone because it lacks the enzymes or gut microbes to use it
senses.definitionCN: 指因缺乏利用植物的酶或肠道微生物、无法仅靠植物维生的食肉动物
senses.example: The domestic cat is an obligate carnivore that needs taurine from meat.
senses.exampleCN: 家猫是专性食肉动物，必须从肉类获得牛磺酸。
senses.why: Physiology, not preference, makes the class: an obligate carnivore would starve on a vegetarian diet.
senses.whyCN: 决定这一类的是生理而非偏好：专性食肉者吃素会饿死。

senses.title: Apex carnivore
senses.titleCN: 顶级食肉者：成年后几无天敌
senses.definition: a carnivore at the top of its food chain that suffers little or no predation itself
senses.definitionCN: 指处于食物链顶端、自身几乎或完全不被捕食的食肉动物
senses.example: The removal of the apex carnivore let the deer herd grow unchecked.
senses.exampleCN: 顶级食肉者的消失让鹿群无限制增长。
senses.why: The label marks position rather than appetite: the top carnivore regulates the levels below it.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签标出位置而非食欲：顶级食肉者调节其下各层。

senses.title: Carnassial shear
senses.titleCN: 裂齿剪切：食肉动物的牙齿构造
senses.definition: a carnivore identified by specialised shearing teeth that slice flesh rather than grind it
senses.definitionCN: 指以专门剪切齿、切割而非研磨肉类的食肉动物
senses.example: The fossil's carnassial teeth show it was a carnivore.
senses.exampleCN: 化石上的裂齿表明它是食肉动物。
senses.why: Anatomy is evidence: paleontologists read the diet of extinct animals from the shape of their teeth.
senses.whyCN: 解剖即证据：古生物学家从牙齿形状读出已灭绝动物的食性。

senses.title: Carnivore guild
senses.titleCN: 食肉集团：共享猎物的竞争者
senses.definition: in community ecology, the set of carnivores in one habitat that partition prey by size, time or hunting method
senses.definitionCN: 群落生态学中指同一生境中按猎物大小、时间或狩猎方式分工的一群食肉动物
senses.example: The carnivore guild splits the night into separate hunting shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 食肉集团把夜晚分成不同的狩猎班次。
senses.why: Competition forces the class to divide resources, so the word becomes a unit of community structure.
senses.whyCN: 竞争迫使这一类分配资源，因此这个词成为群落结构的单位。

senses.title: Carnivorous plant
senses.titleCN: 食虫植物：捕虫并消化吸收
senses.definition: a plant that captures and digests small animals, usually insects, to obtain nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 指捕获并消化小动物（通常为昆虫）以获取养分的植物
senses.example: The pitcher plant is a carnivore that digests insects in its fluid.
senses.exampleCN: 猪笼草是一种在液体中消化昆虫的食肉植物。
senses.why: The word is borrowed for plants because the mechanism is the same: capture, kill and absorb.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被借用于植物，因为机制相同：捕获、杀死并吸收。

senses.title: Human carnivore
senses.titleCN: 人类的食肉者：以肉为主食的人
senses.definition: a person whose diet is based mainly on animal flesh, or a cultural label for meat-centred eating
senses.definitionCN: 指以动物肉为主食的人，或指以肉为中心的饮食文化标签
senses.example: The festival celebrates the region's identity as a land of carnivores.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆庆祝该地区作为食肉者之乡的身份。
senses.why: The zoological label becomes a cultural identity, usually light-hearted rather than clinical.
senses.whyCN: 这个动物学标签变成文化身份，通常轻松而非临床。

senses.title: The order Carnivora
senses.titleCN: 食肉目：分类学上的一个目
senses.definition: in taxonomy, the mammalian order Carnivora, which includes cats, dogs, bears and seals, some of which eat little meat
senses.definitionCN: 分类学中哺乳动物的食肉目，包括猫、犬、熊与海豹，其中有些很少吃肉
senses.example: Not every member of Carnivora is a strict carnivore; bears eat berries.
senses.exampleCN: 食肉目并非每个成员都是严格食肉者；熊也吃浆果。
senses.why: Taxonomy and diet diverge here, which is why the order name can mislead a reader about a species' food.
senses.whyCN: 分类与食性在此分岔，因此目名可能误导读者对该物种食物的判断。

intro.en: Carnivore joins Latin caro 'flesh' with vorare 'to devour', literally 'flesh devourer', and it was fixed in scientific Latin before entering English.
intro.cn: carnivore 由拉丁语 caro「肉」与 vorare「吞食」构成，字面即「吞食肉者」，先在科学拉丁语中定型，后进入英语。

items.en: Caro, carnis meant flesh, especially animal flesh, and it also gives English carnal and carnage.
items.cn: caro, carnis 意为肉，尤指动物肉，它也是英语 carnal 与 carnage 的来源。

items.en: Vorare meant to swallow or devour, the same second element as in herbivore and omnivore.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞咽、吞食，与 herbivore、omnivore 中的后半部分相同。

items.en: Carnivorus was used in modern scientific Latin for flesh-eating animals, and Cuvier's classification is usually credited with popularising it in the early nineteenth century. The exact coining is uncertain.
items.cn: carnivorus 在近代科学拉丁语中用于食肉动物；一般认为居维叶在 19 世纪早期的分类体系推广了它，但确切的造词者存疑。

items.en: English carnivore appears in the nineteenth century, and the exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 carnivore 在 19 世纪出现，确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: Carnivora was fixed as an order name, later creating the awkward fact that some carnivorans are largely herbivorous.
items.cn: Carnivora 被定为目名，后来造成一个尴尬事实：有些食肉目成员其实以植物为主食。

items.en: The nineteenth-century discovery of insect-eating plants extended carnivore to plants, where it remains a common though informal label.
items.cn: 19 世纪对食虫植物的发现把 carnivore 扩展到植物，这一标签至今常用，但属非正式说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vore ending; the near-meaning group separates a diet class from hunting behaviour and taxonomy.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vore 结尾；近义组区分食性类别、狩猎行为与分类学。

entries.definition: An animal that eats plants. It is the opposite diet class, differing only in the first element of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 指以植物为食的动物。它是相反的食性类别，复合词只在第一部分不同。

entries.definition: An animal that eats both plants and flesh. A carnivore may occasionally eat plants without becoming an omnivore in the classificatory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指既吃植物也吃肉的动物。食肉动物偶尔吃植物，并不因此在分类上变成杂食动物。

entries.definition: The adjective form. Carnivore is the noun for the animal, so a plant is described as carnivorous, not as a carnivore in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词形式。carnivore 是动物的名词，因此在正式写作中植物应说成 carnivorous，而不是 carnivore。

entries.definition: One that hunts and kills. A predator may eat plants as well, and a carnivore may be a scavenger that never hunts.
entries.definitionCN: 指猎杀者。捕食者也可能吃植物，而食肉动物可能是从不狩猎的食腐者。

entries.definition: A bird of prey, or in palaeontology a grasping dinosaur. It names a hunting form, not a diet class.
entries.definitionCN: 指猛禽，古生物学中也指具抓握能力的恐龙。它命名狩猎形态，而非食性类别。

entries.definition: An animal that eats mainly insects. It is a narrower diet class that can sit inside carnivory.
entries.definitionCN: 指以昆虫为主食的动物，是更窄的食性类别，可归入食肉范畴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: caro 'flesh' + vorare 'devour': the flesh devourer.
normal.cn: caro「肉」+ vorare「吞食」：吞食肉者。

normal.en: The family runs carnivorous, carnivory, carnassial and the order name Carnivora.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 carnivorous、carnivory、carnassial 以及目名 Carnivora。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: obligate carnivore, top carnivore, large carnivore, carnivore guild.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：专性食肉动物、顶级食肉动物、大型食肉动物、食肉集团。

normal.en: Carnivora is an order, not a diet rule: bears belong to it and still eat berries.
normal.cn: Carnivora 是一个目，不是食性规则：熊属于该目，却仍吃浆果。

normal.en: Carnal and carnage share the caro- root, which is about flesh rather than eating.
normal.cn: carnal 与 carnage 共享 caro- 词根，该词根指肉，而非吃。

abstract.en: Picture a wolf worrying a carcass while the pack waits in a ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狼撕扯尸体，狼群在外圈等待。

abstract.en: Picture a pitcher plant holding a fly in its fluid.
abstract.cn: 想象猪笼草把一只苍蝇泡在液体里。

abstract.en: Picture a fossil jaw with one blade-like tooth standing taller than the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象一块化石颌骨，其中一枚刀状齿高出其余。

examples.en: Large carnivores need wide ranges and abundant prey.
examples.cn: 大型食肉动物需要广阔的活动范围与充足的猎物。

examples.en: The cat is an obligate carnivore and cannot thrive on plants.
examples.cn: 猫是专性食肉动物，无法靠植物良好生存。

examples.en: Carnivorous plants supplement their mineral intake with insects.
examples.cn: 食虫植物用昆虫补充矿物质摄入。

dict_mnemonic.text: carni（肉）+ vore（吃……者）→ 吃肉的 → carnivore 食肉动物

root: 拉丁 caro, carnis「肉」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 carnivorus／carnivore「吞食肉者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a flesh eater, but the boundary shifts: physiology, position in the chain, tooth shape, community role, plants and taxonomy each redraw it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指食肉者，但边界不断移动：生理、链条位置、齿形、群落角色、植物与分类学各自重新划定它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wolf tearing at a carcass while the pack circles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只狼撕扯尸体，狼群在外围。

branches.en: DIET AND PHYSIOLOGY: eating flesh is the base, and inability to use plants makes it obligatory.
branches.cn: 食性与生理：吃肉是基本义，无法利用植物则使它成为专性。

branches.en: POSITION AND COMMUNITY: apex carnivores and guilds describe how the class is arranged.
branches.cn: 位置与群落：顶级食肉者与食肉集团描述这一类的排列方式。

branches.en: EVIDENCE: shearing teeth let palaeontologists read diet from bone.
branches.cn: 证据：裂齿让古生物学家从骨骼读出食性。

branches.en: BOUNDARY CASES: plants and the order Carnivora both stretch the label past its diet meaning.
branches.cn: 边界个案：食虫植物与食肉目都把标签拉伸到食性义之外。

branches.en: CULTURE: human meat eating borrows the zoological word as identity.
branches.cn: 文化：人类食肉借用这个动物学词汇作为身份。

intro.en: Carnivore is the flesh branch of the -vore family, and its stem caro- also feeds words about the body and about slaughter.
intro.cn: carnivore 是 -vore 词族中的「肉」支，其词干 caro- 还衍生出关于身体与屠杀的词。

latinIntro.en: Caro, carnis is a third-declension noun for flesh, vorare a first-conjugation verb for devouring, and -vorus the adjectival form.
latinIntro.cn: caro, carnis 是第三变格的「肉」名词，vorare 是第一变格的「吞食」动词，-vorus 是形容词形式。

items.example: The forest holds three large carnivores.
items.exampleCN: 这片森林里有三种大型食肉动物。

items.example: Carnivorous fish patrol the reef edge.
Carnivory appears in several lizard lineages.
items.exampleCN: 食肉习性出现在好几个蜥蜴谱系中。

items.meaning: a shearing tooth of a carnivore
items.meaningCN: 食肉动物用于剪切的牙齿
items.example: The carnassial pair works like scissors.
items.exampleCN: 那对裂齿像剪刀一样工作。

items.example: Carnivora includes both hunters and berry eaters.
items.exampleCN: 食肉目既包含猎手，也包含吃浆果者。

items.example: The poem contrasts carnal appetite with reason.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗把肉体欲望与理性对照。

items.example: The battlefield was a scene of carnage.
Herbivores and carnivores split the grass crop.
items.exampleCN: 植食动物与食肉动物分食草料。

items.example: The omnivore takes fruit and insects alike.
items.exampleCN: 杂食动物既吃果实也吃昆虫。
